items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: So you went with Harry James then. ... So I went with Harry for the same money... First trumpet player got a hundred.

ctx.x: Tenor saxophone player. I was going into the subway of Jackson Heights, to go into town, and he was coming out of it. And he says, “Hey Jackson, where you going?” I says, “I’m going in town” you know, “and see what’s happening at the Nola studios.” He says, “Harry James is starting — you know Harry from Benny Goodman’s band?” I says, “Well I don’t know him personally.” He says, “He’s rehearsing his first band.” He says, “Go to the Nola Studios and tell them I suggested you talk to him.” See and I did. I went…
Now I’m looking at a sheet from a big band book, from 1938, and it has Red Norvo and it has you listed with Johnny Owens—

items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: So Harry’s father was the band leader and Harry’s mother was the aerialist.

ctx.x: While she’s up on the trapeze, oh my.
